newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Mother Teresa suffers health setback.
newsitem.headline: India's Mother Teresa suffers health setback.

text.p: Doctors treating Mother Teresa said on Monday that they planned a second attempt to correct the 86-year-old nun's irregular heartbeat after she suffered a setback in her recovery from coronary surgery.

Doctors at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner's heartbeat began faltering again on Sunday night, four days after she underwent a procedure called cardioversion to fix the problem.
Hospital administrator A.K. Chatterjee told reporters: "It's a setback in her treatment."
The hospital said in a statement that her team of doctors intended to make a repeat attempt, but had not yet set a date.

"Doctors feel that they should attempt cardioversion one more time and give her the benefit of sinus (regular) rhythm since they know this makes a tremendous difference in her with regard to short-term and long-term prognosis," the hospital said.

The revered Roman Catholic missionary had surgery last month to unblock two coronary arteries, her third such operation in five years. Her recovery has been delayed by her erratic heart rhythm as well as long-standing lung and kidney problems.
Last Wednesday they gave Mother Teresa, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, a mild electric shock to correct her heartbeat.

Doctors said the cardioversion procedure was a success. But a U.S. member of the panel, Dr Patricia Aubanel, said that if Mother Teresa's heartbeat became "chaotic" again, doctors would probably not be able to help her recovery.
The hospital said the recurrence of irregular heartbeats had not damaged Mother Teresa's heart, and she was talkative and had listened to morning mass.

Earlier on Monday, doctors had said Mother Teresa was in stable condition. She slept well overnight despite the erratic heartbeat, took morninig tea and said her prayers an hour later, the hospital said.
Mother Teresa has been keen to get back to her work with the world's poor and sick, which has won her the title "Saint of the Gutters".
Mother Teresa has become increasingly restive as she gained strength and has regularly implored doctors to let her resume her work as head of the Missionaries of Charity religious order.
Doctors had earlier said they hoped Mother Teresa would be home in time for Christmas, but have warned that her recovery would be slow and she may not be as active as before.
